Rasulullaah ﷺ recited Surah Tanzeel Sajdah (Surah) and made such a long Sajdah that people living as far as two miles away arrived there as people started telling each other about the Sajdah. Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) sent a message to her family telling them to come because she was seeing Rasulullaah ﷺ do something she had never seen him do before.
After Rasulullaah ﷺ had lifted his head (from Sajdah), Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! You prolonged your Sajdah so much?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "I prostrated to my Rabb out of gratitude for the Ummah He has granted me. There shall be seventy thousand of them who shall enter Jannah without reckoning." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! You have an Ummah that is large and extremely pure. You should have asked for more for them." This he repeated two or three times when Hadhrat Umar (RA) added, "May my parents be sacrificed for you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ! You have asked a great gift for your Ummah."[^1]
The Gratitude Rasulullaah ﷺ showed when he saw a man Suffering from a Terminal Disease

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by a man suffering from a terminal disease, he dismounted from his animal and made Sajdah. When Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) passed by the man, he also dismounted and made Sajdah and Hadhrat Umar (RA) followed suit when he passed by.[^2]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Thanks Allaah for Returning his Family Members Safely from an Expedition

Hadhrat Ali (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched an expedition comprising of his family members, he prayed, "O Allaah! If You return them to me safely, I owe it to You to thank You as You ought to be thanked." It was not long afterwards that they came back safely and Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "All praise belongs to Allaah for all the bounties of Allaah." "O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" Hadhrat Ali (RA) asked, "Did you not say that if Allaah returned them safely, you owed it to Him to thank Him as He ought to be thanked?" "Did I not just do that?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied.[^3]
